key_insight: The paper introduces the Empathy Applicability Framework (EAF), a theory-driven method that predicts when empathy should be applied to general health queries—enabling models to anticipate, not just react to, empathy needs. This lets AI systems tailor responses more appropriately to patient emotional/contextual cues.
problem_solved: LLMs and clinical NLP systems often lack or inconsistently apply empathy, because existing work focuses on labeling clinician responses rather than anticipating whether a patient query requires empathetic framing; EAF fills that gap by classifying queries for empathy applicability.
method: Develop a theory-driven taxonomy (EAF) that defines when empathy is applicable for general health queries.
Annotate representative general-health queries with applicability labels and contextual tags based on the framework.
Train and evaluate classifiers/heuristics that predict empathy applicability to guide LLM response style or routing.
impact: Anticipatory empathy modeling helps AI/ML practitioners build safer, more patient-centered conversational agents by enabling context-aware response style selection, improving trust and communication in health-related interactions.
visual_elements: Taxonomy diagram showing EAF categories (e.g., clearly applicable, sometimes applicable, not applicable) with short examples
Pipeline flowchart: Query → EAF classifier → Style selector → LLM response
Before/after example pairs illustrating a neutral reply vs. an empathy-aware reply for the same query
Bar chart or heatmap of empathy-applicability distribution across common query types
paper_title: Empathy Applicability Modeling for General Health Queries
paper_authors: Shan Randhawa, Agha Ali Raza, Kentaro Toyama, Julie Hui, Mustafa Naseem
